property.implication: Physical access and land utility can matter more than county demographics.
property.note: Official lookup/topic source only: Obtain survey, title report, plans and physical inspection; retain identifiers privately.

property.metric: Seismic design, site soils, liquefaction and retrofit condition
property.implication: Regional earthquake probability is not a building-collapse probability.

property.implication: Contamination and prior dry-cleaning/fuel uses can impair value.
property.note: Official lookup/topic source only: Obtain Phase I ESA and, if indicated, Phase II privately; issuer risk disclosure is not a site finding.

property.implication: A brand-name tenant does not eliminate uninsured owner loss.

property.metric: Owner liquidity needs, concentration, time horizon and risk tolerance
property.implication: A property-optimal decision may not be owner-optimal.

property.implication: An extension or sale can require approvals that change timing and price.
property.note: Official lookup/topic source only: Review lease and franchise-related consent requirements privately.

property.implication: $20 is the initial covered floor, not a verified current payroll assumption.
property.note: Official lookup/topic source only: Check current DIR/council and local schedules for the actual jurisdiction before tenant underwriting.

property.implication: No store-level demand or market-share value is inferred.
property.note: Official lookup/topic source only: Review private operator reports and a field-verified competitive catchment.

property.note: Official lookup/topic source only: Obtain a current private title/preliminary report and public-record review without exposing identifiers.

risks.implication: Buyer financing and pricing can deteriorate as the certain income term shrinks. Renewal is not automatically landlord-controlled. Mitigation: Map option/notice dates; seek an extension and market bids before the financing window narrows.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: SEC filings disclose franchise payment delays; the actual operator may be weaker than the brand. Mitigation: Verify obligor/guarantor, rent coverage, arrears and security; size a private carrying-cost reserve.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Closures can occur even while the overall chain survives; a profitable brand portfolio need not preserve every site. Mitigation: Obtain unit-level performance and reimage/commitment plans; assess alternative users before conceding rent.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Wage floors and food/energy inflation can reduce a tenant’s ability to absorb rent increases. Mitigation: Underwrite normalized labor and food costs; avoid rent resets that make the location uneconomic.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: County population decline can restrain transaction growth despite nominal menu-price increases. Mitigation: Use flat/negative real-demand cases and verify actual catchment, not county averages alone.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Information and film weakness can reduce nearby daytime demand even as healthcare grows. Mitigation: Diversify demand sources in site underwriting; do not capitalize one strong sector into the entire trade area.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Higher required yields can lower buyer bids independently of tenant performance. Mitigation: Stress exit pricing and discount rates; verify debt maturity and avoid forced-sale timing.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Rent escalations below inflation erode real income; replacement costs can rise faster than NNN reimbursements. Mitigation: Compare real and nominal cash flows; negotiate appropriate bumps without impairing coverage.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Roof, structure, parking, insurance gaps and unreimbursed administration can remain with the owner. Mitigation: Read the lease rather than the marketing label; commission a condition assessment and reserve study.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Vacancy can require carrying costs, tenant improvements, commissions and free rent before income resumes. Mitigation: Model zero-rent periods explicitly and obtain alternative-user bids before expiry.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: A long fixed-rent extension can protect occupancy while surrendering upside or accepting weak credit. Mitigation: Compare extension value with current bids and market-rent reset alternatives; reject value-destructive terms.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: A lease of 35 years or more including written options can constitute a change in ownership. Mitigation: Obtain property-tax counsel before executing an extension or restructuring options.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: City ULA can materially reduce net proceeds above thresholds; it does not apply merely because a listing says Los Angeles. Mitigation: Confirm jurisdiction and closing-date rules; compare after-tax net proceeds, not asking price.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.metric: Tax leakage and failed exchange timing
risks.implication: Recapture, boot, state tax and missed exchange deadlines can reduce investable proceeds. Mitigation: Use private tax basis and a qualified intermediary before closing; evaluate a taxable diversified sale versus replacement-property risk.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.metric: Buyer retrading, financing failure and execution risk
risks.implication: Headline offers may not close; diligence can reveal defects and lenders can reprice. Mitigation: Require evidence of funds/financing, deposits and clear contingencies; maintain a fallback hold plan.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Damage, access loss, customer displacement and smoke can interrupt rent even without building destruction. Mitigation: Check adopted hazard maps, hardening, insurance and rent-abatement clauses; stress prolonged outage.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Regional shaking can damage structures and roads/utilities; repair demand can raise costs. Mitigation: Obtain seismic/soil review, earthquake and rent-loss coverage quotes, and an engineered repair reserve.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.metric: Flood, debris flow and drainage failure
risks.implication: Effective flood mapping and post-fire debris pathways are site-specific; county location cannot resolve them. Mitigation: Review FIRM, local hydrology, elevation and exclusions; do not assume absence of a mapped zone means no risk.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.metric: Insurance nonrenewal, exclusions or slow recovery
risks.implication: Insurance proceeds may arrive late or exclude key perils; lender coverage requirements can force expensive replacement. Mitigation: Review full policies, limits and business-interruption periods; maintain liquidity rather than relying on disaster aid.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Lane reductions and pedestrian detours can hurt a drive-thru or walk-up location before transit benefits arrive. Mitigation: Check agency notices and driveway rights; do not pay for speculative transit uplift today.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: A restaurant site may not permit the desired replacement use, density, parking or drive-thru. Mitigation: Verify zoning, overlays, legal nonconforming rights and entitlement cost before assigning residual land value.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Owner/operator liability can arise from current or historical contamination and delay transfer or financing. Mitigation: Obtain private Phase I/II work and legal allocation of obligations; no environmental clearance is asserted here.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.metric: Title, easement, parking or access defect
risks.implication: Encumbrances can invalidate assumed access, parking counts or redevelopment capacity. Mitigation: Review current title, survey, shared-parking agreements and condemnation records privately.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.metric: Pandemic, civil unrest or utility/cyber outage
risks.implication: Public-health restrictions, unrest or infrastructure failures can combine access loss with tenant cash-flow stress. Mitigation: Stress 12–24 months of interrupted rent plus carrying costs; review force majeure, abatement and security provisions.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Fuel and supply-chain shocks can affect ports, food costs and household spending at the same time. Mitigation: Use combined inflation-plus-low-demand scenarios; avoid treating sector indicators as independent guarantees.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.metric: Drought, extreme heat and water restrictions
risks.implication: Heat raises operating costs and can alter customer behavior; water constraints can affect landscaping and redevelopment. Mitigation: Review local utility rules, equipment efficiency and climate resilience; no numeric loss is inferred.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: One building, one tenant and one region can dominate personal wealth even when property cash flow is stable. Mitigation: Assess private net-worth concentration and cash needs; diversification may justify selling below a theoretical hold value.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Sale proceeds can be reinvested into an equally risky asset, held idle, or exposed to exchange deadlines. Mitigation: Compare after-tax diversified alternatives and fiduciary advice; an exchange is tax deferral, not automatic wealth creation.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: Tourism and Olympics exposure can be temporary and unevenly distributed; construction costs occur before benefits. Mitigation: Underwrite recurring local demand first; assign no permanent event premium without site evidence.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

risks.implication: County statistics, old comparables and mismatched definitions can create false precision. Mitigation: Keep blank unknowns, retain source vintages, test assumptions and independently appraise the actual property.
risks.note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.

decisions.implication: Preserves current income and avoids an immediate taxable sale. Tradeoff: Retains tenant, rollover, hazard and concentration risk; a wasting lease term can reduce marketability. Decision gate: Use when verified net bids do not compensate for conservatively valued remaining cash flows and reserves are adequate.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.metric: Competitive sale before the lease gets shorter
decisions.implication: Can transfer tenant/rollover/hazard risk while remaining term is still financeable. Tradeoff: May sacrifice upside and trigger taxes, transfer charges and prepayment costs. Decision gate: Compare executable net proceeds with conservative hold value and the owner’s diversification/liquidity needs.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: May collect more rent if the tenant performs. Tradeoff: Concentrates negotiation, vacancy and financing risk into a narrow window. Decision gate: Only justify with strong unit coverage, credible renewal intent, ample liquidity and a funded re-leasing plan.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: Can lengthen marketable income without changing ownership. Tradeoff: Weak rent, concessions, options or guarantors can destroy value; long terms can trigger reassessment. Decision gate: Execute only if the risk-adjusted extension premium exceeds concessions and retained risk.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: A stronger lease may broaden the buyer/lender pool. Tradeoff: Extension negotiations consume time and may not improve net price enough to cover costs. Decision gate: Use a value-before/value-after analysis and confirm transfer/consent requirements.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.metric: Wait for tenant renewal, then sell
decisions.implication: Avoids landlord concessions if the tenant exercises a valuable option. Tradeoff: The tenant may decline, demand a reduction or control timing. Decision gate: Track notice deadlines and maintain a sale/hold fallback rather than assuming exercise.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: Balances a longer income term with inflation protection and flexibility. Tradeoff: Reset disputes, caps and tenant affordability can limit protection. Decision gate: Model fair-market-rent procedures, notice timing and realistic coverage.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: May preserve a viable operator and avoid downtime. Tradeoff: A permanent rent cut can outweigh the value of added term. Decision gate: Require unit financials and compare the net present value against replacement tenant and sale paths.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: Could improve rent, credit or use if the location supports another operator. Tradeoff: Downtime, improvements, commissions and entitlement risk can be substantial. Decision gate: Obtain credible replacement-user demand and a funded lease-up budget before relying on this path.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: May unlock higher-value land use where legally and physically feasible. Tradeoff: Construction, entitlement, environmental, leasehold and market risk can overwhelm residual land value. Decision gate: Require title/zoning/environmental clearance, costed plans and preleasing/exit evidence.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.value: Tax tool, not a standalone answer
decisions.implication: May defer eligible federal gain and preserve investable capital. Tradeoff: Strict timing, boot, state rules and replacement-asset concentration can reduce benefits. Decision gate: Use only after private tax analysis and replacement-asset underwriting; arrange intermediary before closing.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: Can reduce single-asset exposure and improve liquidity. Tradeoff: Tax drag and reinvestment risk are real; diversification is not a return guarantee. Decision gate: Compare after-tax risk-adjusted outcomes against continued concentration; obtain fiduciary advice.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: May fund reserves without an immediate sale. Tradeoff: Adds leverage, debt service, maturity and prepayment risk. Decision gate: Stress vacancy cash flow and lender covenants; do not use debt to disguise weak property economics.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: May broaden buyers or spread eligible tax recognition. Tradeoff: Creates buyer credit exposure and delays full liquidity; tax treatment is fact-specific. Decision gate: Require collateral, underwriting and tax/legal review; not assumed available or beneficial.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: Can release some capital while retaining upside. Tradeoff: Governance, control, transfer restrictions and reassessment can be complex. Decision gate: Value the retained interest and minority discount; obtain legal/tax advice before marketing.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

decisions.implication: May align with philanthropic or intergenerational goals. Tradeoff: Irreversibility, liquidity and complex valuation/tax rules make this unsuitable as a default. Decision gate: Only evaluate privately with qualified fiduciary and tax professionals; no personal facts are assumed.
decisions.note: No decision is asserted to maximize personal wealth without private after-tax and liquidity analysis.

This does not reconcile cleanly with the displayed levels or the EDD series. Job levels are excluded from the model; published growth rates remain labeled official forecasts pending raw-workbook review.
